REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 27, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

7A.
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of October 10, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes
7B.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 27, 2016 (COUNCIL).
Register of Demands

8A.
Review and consideration of potential budget expenditure reduction measures (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
8B.
Review and consideration of a proposal for the development of a ballot measure that would place before the Cerritos electorate at the March, 2017 General Municipal Election the question of whether to approve a local sales tax increase (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report

Review and consideration of an informational report of the results so far generated from the community budget priorities survey (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
8D.
Review and consideration of the 2017 City of Cerritos General Municipal Election dates including the potential adoption of resolutions to call the March 7, 2017 election and a proposed one-time consolidation with Los Angeles County special election or introduce an ordinance to change the current scheduled date of the election (COUNCIL).

9.

Review and consideration of a utility agreement with the California Department of Transportation establishing the responsibilities and financial liabilities related to the relocation of the sanitary sewer line on Valley View Avenue in connection with the I-5 Corridor Improvement Project within the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.

13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 27, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Dr. Bill Ebling, First Baptist Church of Fullerton.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by “The Little Raiders.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Victor Manolo, Mayor of the City of Artesia, provided an update report on the
  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) activities.

  Anantha Narayanan spoke regarding the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) that
  are posted to the City’s website and inquired as to the amount required to
  maintain the revenue infrastructure for the auto square and the mall.

  Gail Grossman requested the City Council hear Item 8C on the agenda prior to
  Items 8A and 8B and to vote separately on each item.

  Josh Nass requested the City Council hear Item 8C on the agenda prior to Items
  8A and 8B and to vote separately on each item.

  Marty Grossman encouraged the City Councilmembers to not delay decision-
  making on the items appearing on the agenda.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to consider Agenda
  Item 8C prior to Items 8A and 8B on the agenda and to consider each item
  independently (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  October 10, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of October 10, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 27,
  2016 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 27, 2016 in the
  amount of $4,782,140.17 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of potential budget expenditure reduction measures
  (COUNCIL)

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Josh Nass inquired as to how the City Council can vote on placing a sales tax measure
  and approving a museum when potential budget savings analysis on the CCPA, water
  utility, and power plant has not yet been completed.

  Marlene Rofe inquired as to whether the funds received from the Aria and Sage
  projects will be adequate to support road use maintenance and repair costs.

  Jay Gray inquired if the City Council had addressed cuts in their benefits and
  expressed concerns with the privatization of the water utility. He also suggested
  developing empty parcels of land to raise revenue and encouraged the City Council to
  make a final decision on the public hearing items tonight.

  Anantha Narayanan expressed that the City has not taken measures to address the
  structural deficit and that the City has an actual $20 - $30 million deficit. He
  suggested the City provide a 5-year plan to solve the structural deficit before placing
  a sales tax measure.
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Seema Gupta stated that the City must make changes to address the budget deficit
  before placing a sales tax measure.

  George Shy expressed support for the community survey and encouraged the City to
  focus on the top results. He also expressed concerns with a “sunset clause” on the
  potential sales tax measure.

  Charles Sooter submitted a document for the record. He suggested a method by
  which to evaluate the City’s choices in addressing the budget deficit.

  Marty Grossman inquired as to the City’s public comment procedure and expressed
  concerns regarding Council travel. He expressed concerns with the Council’s lack of
  response to the public comments and a petition that was submitted at a previous
  meeting.

  Deepak Jhaveri expressed concern with the degree of budgetary oversight provided
  by the City Council. He stated that safety and security are the prime concerns of the
  community and there should be more policing on the streets.

  Gail Grossman expressed concern that the first budget meeting was not televised and
  that the City Council has not yet made decisions on addressing the budget deficit.
  She made suggestions for budget cuts including cutting several of the Commissions,
  cutting hours at community centers and the library, reducing the amounts spent for
  City-sponsored events, and reducing management staff at the Sheriff’s station.

  Mel Cortez stated that he would support the sales tax measure under certain
  conditions such as getting rid of the museum and theatre, and for the City to stop
  buying properties. He also suggested a tree maintenance fund, rather than continuing
  to support the Art in Public Places program and the museum.

  Robert Buell expressed support for the proposed sales tax measure, citing the amount
  he and other businesses, such as the auto dealers, pay in sales taxes which go to
  support City services. He also expressed that closing the CCPA would result in
  reduced revenue from local businesses and that homeowners will see the effects of
  closing the Sheriff’s station as increases on their homeowners insurance bill.

  Dileep Thakur expressed concern regarding the proposed sales tax measure and
  encouraged the City Council to work on reducing City expenses wisely and make
  major strategic decisions soon to balance the budget.

  Dr. Afshan Abbasi expressed support for the quality of life services including the
  schools, library, parks and public safety. She suggested forming a community
  committee to address the budget deficit.

  Anju Garg expressed her support for public safety and suggested various ways the
  City could raise revenues other than a sales tax, including renting buildings owned by
  the City and increased fees for use of City facilities.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to give direction to staff to
  eliminate the car allowance for the City Council and any members of staff that receive
  the allowance and replace it with the IRS-approved mileage reimbursement
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Chen, to direct staff to eliminate
  all Commissions and Committees effective July 1, 2017, excluding the Planning
  Commission and the Property Preservation Commission (COUNCIL). The motion
  carried (3 – 2, Edwards, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Review each item presented in the staff report for
  Agenda Item 8A and provide direction, pursuant to a roll call vote, to
  eliminate/reduce these items in the Fiscal Year 17-18 City budget in the event a
  sales tax measure is not placed or does not pass.

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 121 City Manager’s Office
  - Elimination of golf towel give away to community golf events - $3,000
  - Elimination of employee holiday event - $5,000 (COUNCIL).

  Item carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 422 Senior Center
  - Reduction in Program Expenses and Supplies thru reduction in scope of
  programs - $11,200
  - Eliminate senior fitness/wellness series an senior health fair - $9,700
  (COUNCIL).

  Item carried (3 – 2, Edwards, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 441 Recreation Services
  - Reduction staff expenses thru the closure of CPE, Heritage and Library one
  day/week - $21,528
  - Eliminate Festival of Friendship event - $14,370
  - Eliminate Volunteer Recognition Program - $19,100
  - Eliminate Easter Egg Hunt - $6,400
  - Reduce scope of Community Spring Festival - $32,000
  - Eliminate Swim Center Safety Expo -$4,150
  - Eliminate support for Kid’s Fishing Derby - $800
  - Reduce scope of Let Freedom Ring Festival - $47,500
  - Eliminate 9/11 Evening of Remembrance - $7,150
  - Eliminate Community Bike Ride Event - $10,000
  - Eliminate Halloween Festival - $28,500 (COUNCIL).

  Item carried (3 – 2, Edwards, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 451 Community Safety
  - Eliminate Sky Knight Program - $290,000
  - Cerritos Sheriff’s Station conversion to Local Area Station - $3,042,000
  (COUNCIL).

  Item carried (3 – 2, Edwards, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 571 Library
  - Reduce Library operating hours and/or materials, databases, and other services
  - $282,325 (COUNCIL).

  Item carries (3 – 2, Edwards, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: Direction to eliminate/reduce the following items:

  Cost Center 611 Theatre Department
  - Eliminate CCPS Subsidies to community groups - $35,000
  - Reduce scope of CCPA subsidy for City events - $56,100 (COUNCIL).

  Item carried (4 – 1, Edwards “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to research whether the City can charge
  impact fees for vehicles impacting Cerritos roadways.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Solanki, to bring back a report to
  Council on alternatives for the Cerritos Astor Museum and learning center including
  information about the building, the facility, and the impact of obligations going
  forward if the project were to stop. The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration of a proposal for the development of a ballot measure
  that would place before the Cerritos electorate at the March 2017 General
  Municipal Election the question of whether to approve a local sales tax increase
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Anantha Narayanan suggested researching other methods of increasing revenue,
  such as an increase in the document transfer tax and, in the event the sales tax
  measure is placed, to institute an oversight committee to make recommendations
  as to how the funds will be spent.

  Jay Gray spoke in opposition to the proposed sales tax measure stating that the
  proceeds would be used to subsidize the CCPA, museum, power utility, and law
  enforcement at the mall/auto square rather than on the deferred maintenance
  items. He suggested development of the open pads at the Towne Center.

  Josh Nass inquired as to why the $15 million in deferred maintenance was not
  included in the budget and suggested that it be included. He also suggested
  determining final costs on cost center items that were listed “TBD” in the report
  prior to placing a sales tax measure.

  George Shy referred to the on-line survey which stated that residents are in
  support of law enforcement and maintenance services. He suggested making
  those the priority and to make cuts in other areas.
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  Charles Sooter presented options for methods by which the Council can make
  budget priority decisions and urged the Council to consider the social costs and
  other impacts of each cut.

  Deepak Jhaveri spoke in opposition to the one-percent (1%) sales tax expressing
  concerns that maintaining the suggested cuts will not be a priority for future City
  Councils and the City will return to its original deficit position.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to place an up to
  one-percent (1%) sales tax measure, with the conditional language suggested
  by the City Attorney, and with a twenty-year (20) sunset clause, on the ballot
  for the March 7, 2017 General Municipal Election (COUNCIL). The motion carried
  (4 – 1, Solanki “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Ray
  NOES:  Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8C.  Review and consideration of an informational report of the results so far
  generated from the community budget priorities survey (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Tracy Winkler referenced that individuals could have submitted the survey through
  one source, such as at the Library or at the schools.

  Josh Nass spoke regarding the mathematical distribution of the votes.

  Jay Gray spoke about focusing on the “quality of life” enhancements due to Cerritos
  services versus increases to home values and made several other suggestions
  regarding the community survey.

  Dileep Thakur inquired as to how the City proposes to provide services in a cost-
  effective manner.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Pulido, to receive and file the
  report. The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8D.  Review and consideration of the 2017 City of Cerritos General Municipal Election
  dates including the potential adoption of resolutions to call the March 7, 2017
  election and a proposed one-time consolidation with the Los Angeles County
  March 7, 2017 special election or introduce an ordinance to change the current
  scheduled date of the election (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk. A PowerPoint Presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido to approve Option One, consolidating the March
  7, 2017 election with Los Angeles County.

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Chen, to
  introduce Ordinance No. 1009, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE DATE OF THE CITY’S
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION FROM THE FIRST TUESDAY AFTER THE
  FIRST MONDAY IN MARCH OF ODD-NUMBERED YEARS TO THE SECOND
  TUESDAY OF APRIL IN ODD-NUMBERED YEARS (COUNCIL). The motion
  carried (4 – 1, Pulido “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of playground equipment at Brookhaven Park
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent.
  A PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  “Nature” color palette for the playground equipment at Brookhaven Park (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 27, 2016

  liabilities related to the relocation of the sanitary sewer line on Valley View

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Edwards and Mayor Ray.
